How Complete Is Your Map of Mom's Support?

Twelve quick questions about what the family knows and has written down. At the end: what you know, what's still unclear, and what to ask.

Download PDF

Answer yes, no or not sure. This checks how complete the family's picture is. It doesn't measure Mom or the people who help her, and no answer here says whether her arrangement is enough or needs anything added.

  1. Is there a written list of everyone who helps Mom in an ordinary week and what each one does, down to the evening phone call?

  2. Has Mom looked over that list and said, in her own words, what's missing or wrong?

  3. For each line on the list, do you know who it came from and roughly when?

  4. Do you know which tasks only one person does today?

  5. For each of those tasks, do you know who else knows how to do it?

  6. Have you written down every backup arrangement the family mentions, even in passing?

  7. Has each person named as a backup been asked, and is their answer written down?

  8. Are the family's open questions about Mom's week written down in one place?

  9. Have you kept the questions about today separate from the ones about what might come up later?

  10. Have you set apart any question about her health or her medications as one for a professional?

  11. Does each open question have the name of someone who will follow it up?

  12. Has the family agreed what would make you look at the list again?

Answer the questions above and your page builds here.

        What this doesn't do

        It counts what the family knows and has written down, not how Mom is doing or whether her arrangement is enough. A low count means only that some things haven't been asked or put on paper yet, and there's no clock on any of them.

        Ready for the next step?

        You can see which parts of Mom's support the family has on paper and which are still guesses. Keep the page you just copied beside you. The care interview goes through her daily life area by area, including the parts that are fine today, and turns your answers into a Family Care Profile you can bring to any care conversation.
